name: en-docs
description: English business documents, at the length people actually send. The core set measures sentence fragments -- a median of 44 characters -- and this one measures things with paragraphs, quoted replies, signatures and log excerpts. The difference is not cosmetic: over-redaction on a 44-character sample has a denominator of 44, propagation across a thread has nowhere to happen, and a document long enough to be windowed never appears at all. Every name, address, number and identifier here is invented, and vendor-prefixed credentials are deliberately absent so that cloning this repository does not trip a secret scanner. Labels mark what a competent human redactor would remove.

samples.note: A reply chain. The same person is introduced once with a salutation and referred to four more times with nothing to anchor on -- propagation is the only thing that reaches those. The quoted block repeats the address.

samples.note: Negative-heavy: a technical specification with almost nothing to protect. Over-redaction on a document like this is what people actually notice, and the core set has no sample long enough to measure it properly.
samples.annotated:
Rate limiting -- design note

Status: draft
Version 2.1.0

Background

The gateway currently applies a fixed limit of 1000 requests per minute per client, enforced in memory on each node. With 12 nodes in the pool the effective limit is closer to 12000, which is not what the documentation says and not what anybody wants.

Proposal

Move the counter to a shared store with a sliding window of 60 seconds. Each request increments a key derived from the client identifier and the current bucket. Buckets are 5 seconds wide, so a window is 12 buckets and expiry is handled by the store rather than by us.

Trade-offs

A shared store adds a network hop to every request. Measured at 0.4ms on the current hardware, which is 2% of the median request. Acceptable.

A node that cannot reach the store must decide whether to fail open or closed. We propose failing open with a local limit of 1000, on the grounds that a rate limiter is a fairness mechanism rather than a security control, and refusing all traffic during a store outage turns a degraded dependency into an outage of our own.

Rollout

Staging first, then 10% of production for a week. Metrics on the dashboard at https://example.com/docs/ratelimit. Rollback is a configuration flag.

Open questions

Whether the bucket width should be configurable per client. Probably not in the first version.

samples.note: The document contains an instruction aimed at a model. The rules never read it; the model tier must treat it as data. Nothing here is labelled sensitive except the real values, so a pass that obeys the injection scores worse rather than better.

samples.note: Placeholder-shaped text the caller wrote themselves. Restoration treats a response as untrusted, and detection must not treat a document as one either: [[?TEXT:<PERSON_001>]] here is a literal the user typed about a bug, not a mapping to resolve.

samples.note: A contract excerpt. Legal text repeats party names dozens of times, which is where a document-scale over-redaction rate diverges most from a sentence-scale one.

SERVICES AGREEMENT (extract)

This Agreement is made between [[COMPANY_NAME:Globex Corporation]] of [[ADDRESS:1600 Pennsylvania Avenue]], Washington (the "Supplier") and [[COMPANY_NAME:Umbrella Ltd]] (the "Customer").

1. Term

This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for 24 months unless terminated under clause 7.

2. Services

The Supplier shall provide the services described in Schedule 1. [[COMPANY_NAME:Globex Corporation]] shall assign a named account manager; the current appointee is [[PERSON:Michael Chen]], contactable at [[EMAIL:m.chen@example.com]].

3. Charges

Charges are as set out in Schedule 2 and are invoiced monthly in arrears. Payment is due within 30 days. Late payment attracts interest at 2% above base rate.

4. Confidentiality

Each party shall keep confidential all information disclosed by the other which is marked confidential or which ought reasonably to be regarded as confidential. This clause survives termination by 5 years.

5. Data protection

Where [[COMPANY_NAME:Umbrella Ltd]] discloses personal data to [[COMPANY_NAME:Globex Corporation]], the Supplier acts as processor and shall process such data only on documented instructions.

7. Termination

Either party may terminate on 90 days written notice. Notices to the Customer shall be sent to [[EMAIL:legal@umbrella.example.com]] and notices to the Supplier to the account manager named in clause 2.
